extracted.intended_audience: machine learning researchers and practitioners releasing or evaluating trained ML models (particularly those working on human-centered models in computer vision and NLP)
extracted.subtask_description: Create concise 'model cards' that accompany released trained machine learning models, documenting their intended uses, performance characteristics, evaluation procedures, and group-differentiated benchmarked results to improve transparency and responsible use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompany models with documentation of performance characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Released models should be accompanied by documentation detailing their performance characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper recommends that released models be accompanied by documentation that makes clear how the model performs; this documentation should be published alongside the model release so users can judge suitability for their contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide benchmarked evaluation across relevant conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Model cards should provide benchmarked evaluation in a variety of conditions, such as across different cultural, demographic, or phenotypic groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly report evaluation broken down by groups relevant to the application domain (examples given: race, geographic location, sex, Fitzpatrick skin type) so stakeholders can see group-differentiated performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include intersectional group analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Model cards should include evaluation for intersectional groups (e.g., age and race, or sex and Fitzpatrick skin type) that are relevant to the intended application domains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where relevant, report performance on intersectional subgroups (combinations of demographic/phenotypic attributes) rather than only on single-attribute slices, to surface compounded disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose intended use cases and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Model cards should disclose the context in which models are intended to be used and clarify intended use cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State intended applications and use contexts explicitly to minimize usage in contexts for which models are not well suited; this helps prevent misuse or overgeneralization of capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe performance evaluation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Model cards should include details of the performance evaluation procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information on how evaluations were conducted (datasets used for evaluation, metrics, experimental setup, sampling, preprocessing, and any benchmark comparisons) so readers can assess validity and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report quantitative evaluation numbers and other relevant documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Model releases should include detailed evaluation numbers and other relevant documentation alongside the model card.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish the actual quantitative results (e.g., metrics per group and overall) and link to supporting documentation (evaluation data, code, limitations, caveats) to increase transparency and enable informed adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep model cards concise (short documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model cards are intended to be short documents accompanying trained machine learning models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the card to be a concise summary that highlights key performance characteristics, intended uses, and evaluation results so it is easily consumable by stakeholders; link out to fuller reports as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure relevance to intended application domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Model card content (groups evaluated, metrics reported, and contextual information) should be relevant to the model's intended application domains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select demographic/phenotypic factors, intersectional slices, and evaluation criteria that matter for the domain(s) where the model will be deployed, and explicitly state domain relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote transparency and responsible democratization
rubrics_metrics.description: Model cards are proposed as a step toward responsible democratization of machine learning and related AI technology by increasing transparency into how well AI technology works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use model cards to surface limitations, failure modes, and distributional performance so downstream users and stakeholders can make responsible decisions about adoption and deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability beyond computer vision and NLP
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the paper focuses on human-centered models in computer vision and natural language processing, the model cards framework can be used to document any trained machine learning model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same documentation principles (intended use, evaluation breakdowns, procedures, caveats) to models in other domains, adapting group/metric choices to domain-specific concerns.
